messages:
Maria Chen: FYI I drafted a short customer-facing activation/handoff playbook focused on reducing renewal risk — specifically: activation lag, early cost surprises, and dev friction. Sharing here for quick feedback before we send to AE/CS leads.

Maria Chen: Key goals: 1) get a dev PoC calling the model with streaming in 1 day; 2) stabilize p99 latency and errors in 7 days; 3) surface early quality feedback for model/regret.

Maria Chen: Core sections I included: "Quick checklist", "Config snippets (batching/caching/streaming)", "Signals to watch (health + renewal risk)", and "Enablement cadence + feedback capture".

Devon Patel: This looks great. Can you paste the config snippet for batching + streaming? AE teams always want something they can drop in. :+1:

Maria Chen: Sure — short example we give customers for Redwood SDK + recommended settings: 

Maria Chen: ```
# JS example: enable streaming + batching hints
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY})
const res = await client.generate({
  model: 'gpt-open-8k',
  prompt: 'summarize user message',
  streaming: true,
  batch: {
    enabled: true,
    maxBatchSize: 8,
    maxLatencyMs: 50 // tune down for low-latency apps
  },
  cache: {
    prefixCache: true,
    ttlSeconds: 60
  }
})
```

Maria Chen: Notes: recommend `maxBatchSize` 4-16 depending on traffic; `maxLatencyMs` 30-150ms. Use prefix/KV caching for stable prompts (greetings, instruction templates).

Lee O'Connor: Add a tiny HTML/email blurb for CS/AE to send to eng contacts: "We’ll help you get streaming enabled for low-latency UX, set batching targets to match your QPS, and add a small cache to avoid repeat token costs. Schedule a 30-min technical onboarding and we can ship a PoC."

Lee O'Connor: Suggested short checklist for customer: 1) Share expected QPS & latency SLO. 2) Provide representative prompt set. 3) Grant test keys / sandbox env. 4) Join 30-min tech call.

Samir Khatri: Add monitoring hooks we can provision: token burn alerts, p95/p99 latency, 5xx error rate (per-route), and cache hit ratio. Also flag retention of evals for 2 weeks for early quality regressions.

Maria Chen: Good call. I added thresholds: token burn spike >30% week-over-week on first 2 weeks => outreach; p99 >450ms => triage; user-facing 5xx >0.5% => urgent incident.

Devon Patel: For renewal risk scoring, can we map activation metrics to risk tiers? e.g., activation < 1 meaningful API call/day within 14d => high risk; repeated latency incidents => medium?

Maria Chen: Yes — draft rubric in doc:
- High risk: no activity by day 14 OR >2 critical errors in 7d
- Medium risk: activity but <10% of expected QPS or persistent >10% dev support tickets
- Low risk: steady usage, cache hit ratio >30%, p95 within SLO

Samir Khatri: Also capture customer feedback loop: we’ll create a shared GH repo with prompt tests + guardrail checks; CS will request weekly sample of 50 prompts for first 30 days and annotate issues.

Maria Chen: I added that under "Feedback capture" with an example issue template for quality regressions.

Lee O'Connor: Can we add a quick troubleshooting flow for common issues: high latency -> check batching config & model variant -> check kernel/quantization guidance; high cost -> check cache TTLs & logging causing repeated cold prompts; low quality -> share failing prompts & evals.

Maria Chen: Yep — included a 3-step triage flow and triage owners (CS for first contact, SE for config, ML team for model/regressions).

onboard-bot: Reminder: Scheduled "Customer activation check-in" for AcmeCorp on 2026-04-02 15:00 UTC (CS: Maria Chen).

Devon Patel: Final ask — can we make a 1-page PDF to hand to AEs with the checklist + 2 sample config snippets? I can take design on this if you drop the copy.

Maria Chen: I'll slice the existing doc into a 1-pager and paste the copy here by EOD. Thanks for the quick feedback everyone. :raised_hands:
